about.description_short: CNH (NYSE: CNH) serves and advances the people who feed and build a growing world. We are an iron-and-tech company, engineering intelligence, automation, and precision into the machines that move the global economy. Our equipment operates in more than 160 markets, supported by a global team of more than 34,000 people, including engineers, technologists, and industry experts. Our brands - Case IH, New Holland, and STEYR in agriculture; CASE Construction Equipment and New Holland Construction in building - are backed by CNH Capital and complemented by a portfolio of technology and regional brands that together generated $18.1B in revenue in 2025. Building on a legacy of innovation dating back to 1842, CNH has achieved milestones including the first mass-produced tractor, the first twin-rotor combine, and the first factory-integrated precision farming system. Today, we are engineering autonomous and predictive machines that will shape the future of food and infrastructure.

analysis_md:
# CNH — CNH Industrial N.V.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-17. Price $11.60 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $14.51B — in scope under $40B. All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The world's No.2 agricultural-equipment maker (Case IH and New Holland Agriculture), plus CASE/New Holland construction equipment and a large captive Financial Services arm ($23,105M of financing receivables at FY2025-end, per the FY2025 10-K). Deeply cyclical: management described Q2 2026 as "the trough of the agriculture cycle" (Q2 2026 release, 2026-08-03). Consolidated revenues TTM $18,185M (fundamentals.json, +0.6% YoY); Q2 2026 consolidated revenues $4.8B, +2% YoY, net income $141M vs $217M in Q2 2025, adjusted diluted EPS guidance for FY2026 narrowed to $0.41–0.46 (higher end of prior ranges).

## Owner's earnings
Capex is NOT the engine's tagged series — see OVERRIDE. With the filing capex override applied, conservative owner's earnings (OCF − capex − SBC) by fiscal year, from financials_history.csv / dcf_numbers.json:
- FY2023: OCF $907M − capex $1,195M (true filed total; engine fill $1,186M) − SBC $99M → negative; OE/share on the engine series is part of why OE is positive in only **3 of the last 5 years**.
- FY2024: OCF $1,968M − capex $1,186M − SBC $71M = $711M → **$0.56/share** (the 3-yr median year).
- FY2025: OCF $2,538M − capex $1,186M (override fill; true filed total $1,198M) − SBC $45M = **$1,307M → $1.04/share** (base_oe_total_latest_fy / base_oe_latest_per_share in dcf_numbers.json).
- Engine normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): **$0.5643/share**.
- Maintenance definition is not quoted: the engine's computed outputs used here carry the conservative (OCF-based) definition, and the filing's own Industrial Activities free cash flow ($513M in FY2025, 10-K reconciliation) excludes Financial Services OCF, so it is not comparable to the consolidated conservative figure.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct):**
- OCF: FY $2,538M − prior YTD (H1 2025) $934M + current YTD (H1 2026) $180M = **TTM $1,784M**
- Capex: **TTM $1,186M** — all three legs filled by the capex override, prorated by days (both YTD legs $588.1M over 181 days; they cancel, leaving the annual override value)
- SBC: FY $45M filed − prior YTD $22.3M (override-prorated) + current YTD $22.3M (override-prorated) = **TTM $45M** (CNH tags SBC only annually — see OVERRIDE)
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **1,242M**
- **TTM OE total $553M → base OE/share $0.4452** (base_source: ttm_json)

## OVERRIDE — capex (filing) and SBC (filing, TTM mechanics only)
- **The gap:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:capex` — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every candidate tag (the last filed PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets value is FY2016, $2,134M). CNH now reports capex only as two consolidated cash-flow lines the engine does not read. Under the bounded authority, judgment.json carries `capex_override = {value: 1186000000, kind: "filing"}` — the FY2024 (median-year) total from the FY2025 10-K Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows: "Expenditures for property, plant and equipment and intangible assets, excluding assets under operating leases" $543M / $536M / $644M (2025/2024/2023) plus "Expenditures for assets under operating leases" $655M / $650M / $551M — totals **$1,198M / $1,186M / $1,195M**. Including operating-lease equipment matches the old PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets definition and is conservative — that equipment is a real recurring cash cost of the leasing fleet. The single-value fill understates true FY2023 capex by $9M and FY2025 by $12M (~0.5% of those years' OE, slightly aggressive — noted in the override's reason, not hidden); FY2024 is exact. In band (0.1×–10× of the last filed $2,134M; override_checks out_of_band: false).

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-to-narrow
Justification: No.2 global ag-equipment franchise (Case IH + New Holland, ~12–14% global share vs Deere's ~18–20%) with a real dealer network, captive finance arm and a parts/service installed base — but returns prove it is narrow, not wide: ROE fell from 28.1% (FY2023) to 16.2% (FY2024) to 6.6% (FY2025), i.e. at/below cost of capital at the trough, and gross margin (31.8% / 32.7% / 31.5% for FY2023/24/25 on total revenues incl. Financial Services, fundamentals.json) is defended by mix, not pricing power — Agriculture net sales fell 11.5% in FY2025 with North America down 26.4% (FY2025 10-K). The roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is unavailable for the recent years (debt tags blank — see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK), so the moat rests on the ROE path and margins quoted above; on that evidence a moat above 4 would need returns through the cycle that CNH has not shown. Deere's integrated precision ecosystem is stronger; Raven gives CNH a credible but not leading tech stack.
- FOR: #2 global ag equipment share (~12–14%) via Case IH and New Holland dual brands; global dealer network plus captive Financial Services ($23.1B financing receivables) that finances a large share of its own sales; installed-base parts and service annuity across a long-lived fleet; Raven precision-ag technology stack and full-line breadth (ag + construction).
- AGAINST: Deere's stronger precision ecosystem, brand and pricing power, with AGCO/Kubota pressure from both ends; pure cyclicality — farm-income-driven volumes, FY2025 Agriculture sales −11.5% (North America −26.4%), ROE 28.1% → 6.6% in two years; tariff exposure and South America weakness compressed Agriculture adjusted EBIT margin to 5.2% in Q2 2026 (Q2 2026 release); thin equity under a large captive-finance balance sheet — consolidated net debt $23,427M at FY2025-end (mostly Financial Services, but the risk is CNH's).
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:capex / OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex**: resolved by the filing override — see OVERRIDE for the gap, the sourced per-year figures, and the measured impact (base $1.5056 → $0.5643 on the median basis).
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 10 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above. Note CNH's OCF is H2-weighted (H1 2026 OCF $180M vs FY2025 $2,538M), so the TTM base is a trough figure, not a run-rate gift.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share $1.04 vs 3-yr median $0.56): both ends are working-capital artifacts of the cycle — FY2023 OE was crushed by a $2,268M build in trade/financing receivables (OCF $907M despite net income $2,275M), FY2025 OE was flattered by the reverse (inventory liquidation +$749M and receivables +$708M into OCF despite net income of only $510M). The median ($0.56) sits between a WC-build year and a WC-release year; the TTM base ($0.4452) is used as the least-distorted current reading, and the median-base run is reported in the method range — both are Tier D.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2025): 2023 — net income $2,275M vs OCF $907M, driven by the $2,268M receivables build and a $535M deferred-tax drag, partly offset by $911M of provisions (FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement). 2025 — net income $510M vs OCF $2,538M: net income absorbed non-cash charges detailed in the 10-K ($313M writedowns of financial assets, a $172M non-cash IPR&D impairment from the Raven/Bennamann acquisitions, a $62M impairment of investments in unconsolidated affiliates — together in "Other non-cash items" of $647M), while OCF was lifted by working-capital release (inventories +$749M, receivables +$708M). The OCF-based conservative OE is the series used throughout; the divergence is cycle/WC mechanics plus identified one-offs, not a hidden earnings-quality break.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years; positive only 3 of 5 years with true capex): real cyclicality, handled by the TTM base, bear-weighted probabilities (15/30 on super bear/bear), and sizing the verdict to the conservative end.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count −2.79%/yr): already credited via the share-count growth adjustment in the blend; not double-counted in the verdict. Diluted shares: 1,251M (FY2025) → 1,242M (H1 2026 YTD).
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK**: stated from the filing (FY2025 10-K, net-debt reconciliation at Dec 31, 2025): consolidated total debt $26,853M, cash and equivalents $2,578M plus restricted cash $651M, **consolidated net debt $23,427M** — of which Financial Services net debt is $21,402M, funding $23,105M of financing receivables, and **Industrial Activities net debt is only $2,025M**. The consolidated OE base therefore carries a finance company's leverage against an industrial's cash flows; the engine can give no leverage verdict (net_debt_to_normalized_oe: null in diagnostics), and this is one reason confidence is low rather than medium.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The investable question on CNH is cycle timing, not this DCF: at trough OE the stock screens expensive on owner's earnings ($11.60 vs weighted IV@15% $2.76), but trough OE is exactly what a buyer of a cyclical is supposed to look through. The honest statement of what the model can and cannot say: even the super-bull scenario (1.25× trough base, +7% start) yields only 8.47% IRR at $11.60, and the latest-FY OE/share of $1.04 — a WC-release year — capitalized at the base path would still not clear 15%. A bull case here needs mid-cycle OE/share well above $1.04 sustained, i.e. a full ag upcycle with margin recovery, which is a forecast about farm income and Deere-era pricing, not something in the filings yet. Q2 2026 showed stabilization (+2% revenue) but Agriculture adjusted EBIT margin fell to 5.2% — the recovery is not in the numbers.
- The preliminary zero-capex run (weighted IRR 14.26%, near Tier B) is a clean example of why the data gate exists: ~$1.19B/yr of real capex was invisible to the tag set, and it moves the answer by ~9pp of IRR.
- Balance-sheet risk is mostly Financial Services: $21.4B of FS net debt against receivables is normal captive-finance structure, but credit losses already produced a $313M writedown of financial assets in FY2025 — in a farm downturn, FS is where the tail risk sits.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 5.33% on the TTM base; 6.10% on the median base — D either way, and D in every individual scenario)
- Confidence: **Low** (cyclical trough base, consolidated industrial+finance OE, leverage not engine-verifiable)
- One-liner: Cyclical No.2 ag/construction equipment maker with a captive finance arm, moat 4/10 — at $11.60 it clears nothing: weighted IRR 5.3% on the TTM trough base (IV@15% $2.76), Tier D in every scenario; it would need to trade near $2.76 to clear a 15% hurdle on trough owner's earnings.
